# ◆ ORPHEUS

multi-service player. desktop (electron: macos, windows, linux) and ios (swiftui remote control for paired desktop players, plus local playback of files served by a desktop player). One queue, playlists and history across local files and the services below.

## ◆ STATUS

- local files, drag and drop, folders: implemented, covered by end-to-end tests
- queue, history (appended after 30 s or at track end), playlists, session: implemented. The session starts empty on every launch and is never restored.
- google drive: library and playback implemented, tested with fakes, needs an account. Files named `.741` under the music root are read as read-only records (house files). They are not written back.
- spotify: library and playback implemented, tested with fakes. Needs a premium account. Playback needs the Widevine build.
- apple music: library and playback implemented, tested with fakes. Needs a developer account.
- soundcloud: library and hls playback implemented, tested with fakes.
- tidal: login, library, search, playlist reads and playlist writes (official API mode) implemented. Endpoints are not yet verified against the live API. Playback in official API mode is covered by fake tests only. Playback in web mode is not implemented and fails with an explicit error.
- transfer of tracks between services: implemented. Matches by ISRC, then by text, with a score and an ask dialog.
- output picker and local outputs: implemented
- AirPlay receiver (AirPlay 1, audio only, desktop): implemented
- phone server (desktop serves files imported on the phone over http, for a room or a sonos target): implemented
- LAN server on desktop (discovery, websocket, pairing): not implemented. The desktop does not serve the LAN protocol yet, so iOS remote control does not reach a desktop yet. iOS discovery and client are implemented against fakes.
- iOS app: implemented against fakes. Not run on a device for the current branch.
- windows and linux packages: defined in CI, not built or run yet.

## ◆ DATA AND SECRETS (today and target)

- desktop state (playlists, smartlists, settings) and history: files in the app's user-data folder, written atomically. Target: `playlist`, `item`, `history` and `setting` records in `collection.741`.
- artwork and waveform caches: local, safe to delete.
- secrets (OAuth tokens, user tokens): Electron safeStorage, never in json and never logged. The iOS pairing token is in the keychain.
- Target per format.md: settings are `setting` records with app `orpheus`. The Orpheus queue and the LAN pairing token hashes stay local.

## ◆ SERVICE SETUP

Service client ids come from settings or the desktop `.env` file. A missing id shows the service as `setup` in the services view. Environment names and registration steps are in the section below.

client ids are read from settings or `desktop/.env`, never committed. missing id -> service shows `setup` in the services view.

## ◆ GOOGLE DRIVE

- status: implemented · fakes · account
- register: google cloud project · enable drive api · oauth consent screen · client type `desktop app`
- test user: add the account in the consent screen (testing mode)
- scope: `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.readonly`
- limits: library lists root folders only · folder walk cap `maxFolders` (default 5000)
- playback: range proxy in main, `orpheus-gdrive` protocol
- path resolve: music root folder id → relative path walked by name, one `files.list` per missing segment
- path index: hits only, persisted in state (`index`, `changesToken`), max 20000 entries, cleared when full
- changes: `changes.list` from the stored start token, read at most every 30 s during a resolve; token 400/404/410 resets token and index
- source order per track: `local` · `mount` · `api` (default); unknown or repeated kinds are dropped
- playback: `orpheus-gdrive://file/<id>` serves the first source of the order that answers: `mount` = file under the Drive-for-desktop root at the same path as in My Drive (path from parent walk, cached per folder), served with Range; `api` = Drive stream. `local` has no probe yet and is skipped
- UNVERIFIED: mount path mapping against a real Drive-for-desktop mount (`My Drive` folder name, shared drives not mapped); parent walk against the real API
- house files: `.741` files under the music root (`gdriveDirect.houseFiles`, default on when enabled) are read with the collection reader and added to the collection as read-only records; found via the mount when the root resolves onto it, else the API (downloaded to the cache). Re-read on the change feed (a `.741` file, a removal or a folder change), on a music root change, and every 30 s poll. Records are not written back; with a live agent a removed house record stays until the next read
- download cache: `<userData>/gdrive-cache/<fileId>.<format>`, limit `cacheLimitMb` (LRU by mtime). Playback checks the cache first. Prefetch: on every queue change (`gdrive:queue`), the first `prefetchCount` Drive tracks of the queue that are neither cached nor reachable through the mount are downloaded
- UNVERIFIED: house file discovery and reload against real Drive (mount root resolution for the root folder itself, change feed names); prefetch and cache downloads against the real API; eviction under real sizes
- not yet: collection status glyph, settings UI for `houseFiles` and `prefetchCount` (settings view only has the existing fields)

## ◆ TRANSFER

- scope: a source track (any service, local, drive) dropped on a target playlist becomes the target service's track
- main: `desktop/src/main/transfer/` · pure parsing and scoring in `text.ts` and `score.ts`
- order per track: remembered decision · isrc lookup (`lookupByIsrc`, when the source has `isrc` and the setting is on) · text search `artist title`, second try with the title alone
- score 0..1: title 0.5 · artist 0.25 · duration 0.25 · missing artist or duration counts as neutral
- caps: no artist in common < 0.6 · title below 0.6 < 0.6 · differing version tags (remix, edit, extended, radio, live, remaster, ...) max 0.85
- auto-accept at or above the auto-accept line (default 0.92) with matching version tags · ask at or above the ask line (default 0.6) · below it: not found
- ask: at most 5 candidates, best first · pick · skip · search manually · preview when the target has a playback backend
- batch: progress bar · cancel keeps the rest unresolved · summary with the not-found list and copy
- cache: `desktop-transfer.json` (schema 1) · auto matches and user decisions per source uid and target · newer schema is left unchanged
- options: Settings > Sources & Services > Transfer · thresholds, ISRC first, duration tolerance, always ask, remember decisions, clear cache
- ipc: `transfer:resolve` · `transfer:search` · `transfer:decide` · `transfer:clearCache` · renderer `resolveTransfer(tracks, target)` implements `TransferResolver`
- tests: unit (`text`, `score`, `cache`, `matcher`, renderer `state/transfer`) · e2e `e2e/transfer.spec.ts` (dialog states, seeded)

## ◆ LAN PROTOCOL v1

binding for desktop + ios. types live in `desktop/src/shared/lan.ts`.

## ◆ DISCOVERY

- mdns service `_orpheus741._tcp`
- txt: `id` (deviceId) · `name` · `v=1` · `platform` (mac | win | linux)

## ◆ TRANSPORT

- websocket `ws://<host>:<port>/ws` · json text frames
- every message: `{ "type": string, "id": string, "payload": object }`
- reply: `{ "type": "result", "id": <request id>, "payload": { "ok": true, "data": ... } }` or `{ "ok": false, "error": { "code": string, "message": string } }`
- error codes: `unauthorized` · `bad_pin` · `rate_limited` · `version` · `unknown_type` · `bad_payload` · `not_available`
- first message within 5 s or the socket closes

## ◆ HANDSHAKE

1. client -> `hello` `{ v: 1, deviceId, name, token? }`
2. server -> `result` `{ ok: true, data: { v: 1, deviceId, name, paired: boolean } }`
3. not paired: client -> `pair.request` `{}` · target shows a 6-digit pin, valid 120 s
4. client -> `pair.confirm` `{ pin }` -> `{ token }` (32 random bytes, base64url)

- open pairing window: the user opens it on the target (Devices, Settings > LAN, shortcut) · shows a 6-digit pin, valid 120 s · "New PIN" replaces it · close or expiry invalidates it
- while the window is open, `pair.request` reuses the shown pin (no new pin)
- pair QR: `orpheus741://pair?h=<host>&p=<port>&id=<deviceId>&n=<name>&pin=<pin>` · `formatPairUri`/`parsePairUri` in `shared/lan.ts` · carries the pin, so it is valid only while the window is open (120 s)
- 5 wrong pins -> `rate_limited` for 60 s (also locks the window)
- server stores only sha-256 of tokens · compares in constant time
- every other type before pairing -> `unauthorized`
- paired devices can be listed + revoked on the target
- revoke closes that device's open socket with close code `4401`, reason `unauthorized`; the controller drops the stored token on that close and removes the device at once
- a controller keeps one idle socket (hello with token, no commands) per discovered paired peer; it counts as control only after its first command

## ◆ COMMANDS (client -> server)

| type | payload | data |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `state.get` | `{}` | `PlayerState` |
| `player.play` · `player.pause` · `player.next` · `player.prev` | `{}` | `{}` |
| `player.seek` | `{ ms }` | `{}` |
| `player.volume` | `{ value }` 0..1, absolute | `{}` |
| `player.volumeStep` | `{ direction }` 1 up, -1 down; the controlled device applies the key rules (100 % hold) | `{}` |
| `player.shuffle` | `{ on }` | `{}` |
| `player.repeat` | `{ mode }` off, all, one | `{}` |
| `player.playTracks` | `{ tracks: TrackRef[], startIndex }` | `{}` |
| `player.playRemoteUrl` | `{ url, title, artist?, durationMs? }` · `url` http(s) on a private IPv4 host (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, 169.254/16), no credentials, max 2048 chars | `{}` · plays on the current output (local chain or Sonos; Sonos fetches the url itself, so http only) · `bad_payload` for other hosts or schemes |
| `queue.add` | `{ tracks, position }` next, end | `{}` |
| `queue.move` | `{ from, to }` | `{}` |
| `queue.remove` | `{ index }` | `{}` |
| `queue.clear` | `{}` | `{}` |
| `output.list` | `{}` | `{ outputs: OutputDevice[] }` |
| `output.set` | `{ id }` | `{}` |
| `playlists.list` | `{}` | `{ playlists: { id, name, count }[] }` |
| `playlists.get` | `{ id }` | `Playlist` |
| `history.list` | `{ limit, before? }` | `{ entries: HistoryEntry[] }` |
| `search` | `{ q, providers? }` | `{ tracks: TrackRef[] }` |
| `stream.url` | `{ uid }` | `{ url, expiresAt }` |
| `waveform.get` | `{ uid }` | `{ peaks: number[], durationMs }` · 800 peaks 0..1 from the waveform cache · `not_available` when no overview is cached yet (the desktop analyses a track when its strip shows it) · providers `local`, `minos`, `gdrive`, `gdrive-mount` |
| `library.sources` | `{}` | `{ sources: { id: 'minos' \| 'own' \| 'history', name, count \| null }[] }` |
| `library.children` | `{ sourceId, nodeId? }` root when `nodeId` is absent | `{ nodes: { id, name, kind: folder \| playlist \| smartlist, count \| null }[] }` |
| `library.tracks` | `{ sourceId, nodeId?, offset, limit }` limit 1..500 | `{ tracks: TrackRef[], total }` |

- library: `minos` = MINOS tree (folders, playlists, smartlists; ids are MINOS node ids) · `own` = own playlists `pl:<id>` and smartlists `sl:<id>` at the root · `history` = flat, `nodeId` absent
- tracks are wire-trimmed (no paths, no artwork urls); the tree is read per node, lazily

## ◆ EVENTS (server -> client)

- `state` -> `PlayerState`, on every change · position at most 1/s · no `id` reply
- `output.changed` -> `{ outputs }`

```ts
interface PlayerState {
  deviceId: string
  playing: boolean
  track: TrackRef | null
  positionMs: number
  positionAt: number      // server epoch ms of positionMs
  volume: number
  shuffle: boolean
  repeat: 'off' | 'all' | 'one'
  queue: TrackRef[]
  session: TrackRef[]
  outputId: string | null
}
interface OutputDevice { id: string; name: string; available: boolean; note?: string }
```

## ◆ AIRPLAY

AirPlay 1 (RAOP) audio receiver. Audio only, ALAC 44.1 kHz 16 bit stereo. Code: `desktop/src/main/airplay/`. Design and licenses: NEXT.md "◆ AIRPLAY RECEIVER".

- name: `settings.airplay.name`, default `settings.deviceName`
- TCP: RTSP/1.0 on the advertised port (OPTIONS, ANNOUNCE, SETUP, RECORD, SET_PARAMETER, GET_PARAMETER, FLUSH, TEARDOWN)
- UDP, three ports per session, returned in SETUP: audio (RTP, payload 96), control (resend requests to the sender's `control_port`, retransmits in), timing (answers the sender's requests with NTP-style replies)
- audio is AES-128-CBC; the AES key arrives RSA-wrapped in ANNOUNCE (AirPort key from shairport-sync, see `airport-key.ts`)
- settings (`airplay` in settings): `enabled` (default true) · `name` · `passwordSet` (RAOP digest, user `iTunes`; the password itself is in the secret store under `airplay-password`, sent once in a save, never returned) · `latencyMs` (default 2000, clamped to 500..4000). A save restarts the receiver only when one of these changed (`controller.ts`)
- events for the playback side: PCM (interleaved s16 stereo, 44100) and `start` / `stop` / `volume` (dB) / `artwork` / `metadata` (DMAP title, artist, album from SET_PARAMETER; `progress` lines as position and duration ms)
- Sonos route: the stream token (`LAN_STREAM_TOKEN_TTL_MS`, 1 h) is renewed every 10 min while the session plays (`AIRPLAY_TOKEN_RENEW_MS`). Sender volume maps -30..0 dB linearly to the room's 0..100 (-144 = 0) only during a Sonos session; the room's volume from before is written back at the end (`sonos-volume.ts`)
- quit: mDNS goodbye, then the sockets close
- macOS: the first mDNS publish and the first UDP send to the LAN trigger the Local Network prompt. Denied: the log shows `raop: local network unavailable (EHOSTUNREACH)` and senders do not find the device. Re-enable in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Local Network, then restart Orpheus
- firewall: incoming connections to Orpheus must be allowed when the macOS application firewall is on

## ◆ PHONE SERVER (iOS)

- off by default · Settings > Phone server · port 0 = auto · link lifetime 15 min, 1 h, 4 h or 24 h
- serves only the files imported on the phone (library > PHONE), nothing else
- `GET` · `HEAD /f/<fileId>?t=<token>` · byte ranges (206) · 416 for bad ranges · `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`
- one token per file: 32 random bytes, valid for the lifetime, sha-256 digest only on the phone, constant-time check; a new link replaces the old one
- 401 bad or expired token · 404 unknown file · 405 other methods
- "Send to" on a phone file: optional `output.set` (Sonos rooms are `sonos:<uuid>` in `output.list`), then `player.playRemoteUrl` with the link (private IPv4, http)
- runs while the app is in the foreground; iOS suspends it otherwise
